newsitem.title: KENYA: Power company lifts Nairobi bourse.
newsitem.headline: Power company lifts Nairobi bourse.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index rose 13.53 points to stand at 3017.19 on Wednesday driven by strong gains in Kenya Power & Lighting Company Ltd, brokers said.
Market officials said turnover was posted at 8.661 million shillings on 228,172 shares compared to 58.139 million shillings on 713,924 shares on Tuesday.
Kenya Power & Lighting Co, in which there also was heavy trading on Tuesday, was active on the special lots board.

The company is still a power monopoly in Kenya. It was not immediately known why its shares were sought after, especially after it started rationing electricity supply in order to meet demand while it repairs one key power station.
The company has said it will ration power until December and company has said it is seeking funding for investment projects.
"The market is subdued. This is not good as it is having a negative effect on some counters," a senior broker said.
Nation Printers & Publishers fell a shilling to 105, Kenya Airways traded 48,608 shares at 10.50, 10 and 10.10 from 10.15 while Uchumi Supermarket was unchanged at 38.50.
Brooke Bond was traded at 177, Sasini Tea & Coffee at 51 while Rea Vipingo traded 11,550 shares at 10.90 from 11.
Barclays Bank rose 2.0 to 104, Kenya Commercial Bank gained to 52.50 from 52 and Standard Chartered Bank rose to 45.40 from 45.
Officials said foreign investors traded 2,500 shares of National Industrial Credit at 41.50 and 2,000 shares of Firestone East Africa Ltd at 24.50.
